title: Bhishma Parva (the Gita re-read in place, 6 sessions)
hook: Arjuna is given a divine eye to see Krishna's universal form, and among the faces rushing into it are names the blind king knows.
tomorrow: Bhishma Parva (the Gita re-read in place, 6 sessions)

segments.voice: Yesterday Arjuna argued that Krishna was born after the sun, and Krishna answered: I know my births, and you don't. Your line: better your own duty, done imperfectly.

Two people in this story are given eyes they weren't born with. One is Sanjaya, who sees the whole battlefield from the palace so he can tell the king. The other is Arjuna, who in the eleventh chapter of the Gita asks to see Krishna as he truly is, and is told his ordinary eyes can't do it. So Krishna gives him a divine eye. And then there's us, listening, because the one describing Arjuna's vision is Sanjaya, speaking to a blind father. Session five of six: the vision, heard from inside the palace.
screen: `EYES THEY WEREN'T BORN WITH` → `ARJUNA GETS A DIVINE EYE` → `SANJAYA TELLS THE BLIND KING`

segments.voice: Arjuna sees a form with countless faces and eyes, a light like a thousand suns rising at once, the whole universe gathered in one body. In the Gita it's Sanjaya who says this to Dhritarashtra. Then the vision turns. Arjuna sees the warriors of the war rushing into terrible mouths, like rivers racing to the sea, like moths into a flame. And he names them. The sons of Dhritarashtra. Bhishma. Drona. Karna. Our own warriors too. Now hear it from where the king sits. He refused to watch this war. He asked only to be told. And here, in the middle of a teaching about God, Sanjaya tells him his own sons are among the faces disappearing into those mouths. Arjuna, shaking, asks: who are you? Krishna answers: I am Time, grown mighty, the destroyer of worlds. Even without you, none of these warriors will survive. They are already slain by me. Be only the instrument. Then he names them again: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna. Read alone, this chapter is a vision of the divine. Read in place, it's also a forecast, spoken over the heads of real men standing in their ranks, waiting. Bhishma is one of them; the book named for him has already told us he will fall. At the end, Arjuna, terrified, asks to see his friend's familiar face again. Krishna takes his gentle form, and Arjuna says: now I'm myself again.
screen: `A THOUSAND SUNS AT ONCE` · `THE WARRIORS RUSH INTO THE MOUTHS` · `I AM TIME. BE THE INSTRUMENT.` · then, large: `THE FAMILIAR FACE AGAIN`

segments.voice: Let your gaze go soft and widen your attention for a breath or two: the room, the building, the street, the sky over it. Then come back, gently, to one familiar thing near you, a cup, a chair, your own breath, and stay there. Arjuna saw everything and then asked for the familiar face; both are allowed, and if you pray, your prayer can rest there too.
Bhishma Parva. The book whose grandsire stands in the ranks while Arjuna's vision names him among those Time has already taken.
Your line: now I'm myself again. After the vision of Time, a friend's face was enough. That's day eight hundred twenty-three.

chat.says: In the Gita, why does Arjuna ask Krishna to go back to his usual form?
options: Seeing Time take the warriors terrified him; he longed for his friend's face.
The vision bored him, and he just wanted to get back to the battle.
He thought the vision was a trick and wanted proof it was real.
chat.meaning: In Gita 11, Arjuna sees the warriors entering the mouths of Time. Terrified, he asks for Krishna's gentle form and says: now I'm myself again.

Sanjaya.meaning: the king's counselor, who sees the battle and tells it

Dhritarashtra.meaning: the blind king, hearing his own sons named in the vision

Jayadratha.meaning: a Kaurava ally, named among the warriors in the vision

Karna.meaning: Kunti's first son, fighting on the Kaurava side
